text:
Tara (CSOps): noticing some customers reported getting two onboarding emails yesterday afternoon. runner shows duplicate sends for survey+welcome on ~34 accounts. anyone else seeing schedule jitter?
Evan (Scheduling): I saw anomalous timing in the scheduler logs around 14:03 UTC where cron-worker A retried the same job id after a transient DB lock. could be the retry logic + insufficient idempotency.
Tara (CSOps): samples: ```
2026-04-02T14:03:12Z job_enqueue: job_id=job-7743 acct=AC-4412 route=onboard-welcome
2026-04-02T14:03:14Z db: deadlock on jobs.queue, retrying
2026-04-02T14:03:14Z job_enqueue: job_id=job-7743 acct=AC-4412 route=onboard-welcome
2026-04-02T14:03:15Z worker: processed job-7743 -> send_email(welcome)
2026-04-02T14:03:16Z worker: processed job-7743 -> send_email(welcome)
```
Maya (Data): that looks like job_id was identical but dedupe-key didn't get persisted before retry. our idempotency lookup reads job_id from jobs.idempotency table, but the write is after enqueue. a retry in <2s window can re-enqueue before idempotency record exists.
Omar (Support): support ticket queue shows 34 accounts with duplicate sends between 14:03-14:10 UTC, mostly on EU region. customers are annoyed but not critical. we should fix fast to avoid spam.
Evan (Scheduling): short-term mitigation: add a pre-enqueue idempotency write (optimistic insert) so retry won't re-enqueue same job_id. low-risk change. long-term: make enqueue + idempotency an atomic DB transaction or switch to leader-ordered queue.
Tara (CSOps): ok owners? Evan -> patch enqueue to optimistic idempotency insert (staging dry-run). Maya -> produce list of affected accounts + dedupe whether they also received survey. Omar -> customer comms for affected accounts. Tara -> monitor duplicate-send-rate and open runbook note. target: patch + backfill within 8 hours.
SchedulerBot: scheduled dry-run for enqueue-change on staging at 2026-04-02T18:00:00Z (run=stg-212) :gear:
Evan (Scheduling): patch pushed to staging, pre-enqueue insert in place. running dry-run now.
Maya (Data): query for affected accounts: ```sql
select acct_id, count(*) as sends from emails where template in ('welcome','onboard-survey') and ts between '2026-04-02T14:00:00Z' and '2026-04-02T14:15:00Z' group by acct_id having count(*) > 1;
-- returns 34 rows
```
Maya (Data): exporting CSV s3://redwood-cs/duplicates/2026-04-02/dup-onboard-34.csv and adding a column already_contacted boolean by joining to outbound events. 22 had survey_sent=true (duplicates), 12 were welcome-only dupe.
Omar (Support): drafting note: "Small duplicate email sent due to transient scheduling retry; no security impact. If you received multiple Welcome emails you can ignore the extra one." will send to affected AMs + optional customer message.
Evan (Scheduling): staging dry-run succeeded. idempotency insert prevented second enqueue in test. running a canary to production for 2 nodes.
SchedulerBot: canary deploy started (canary_id=can-303) at 2026-04-02T18:20:00Z
Tara (CSOps): about backfill/reconciliation: should we cancel duplicates or leave them? i propose: 1) do not cancel emails already sent; 2) for survey sends, avoid re-sending if survey_sent flag exists; 3) record duplicate_tag on accounts for outreach if customers report confusion.
Maya (Data): agreed. i'll run a reconciliation job to mark the 34 accounts with duplicate_tag and create a filtered list of accounts where survey_sent=false so we can enqueue only the missing survey.
Evan (Scheduling): running reconcile script with safety window 72h and idempotency checks: ```python
# pseudo
for acct in candidates:
  if not has_event(acct,'survey_sent'):
    enqueue('survey', acct, meta={'source':'reconcile-2026-04-02'})
```
Evan (Scheduling): reconcile results: re-enqueued surveys for 8 accounts (those missing survey_sent), left 26 as-is. all re-enqueues tagged with source metadata.
Omar (Support): sent comms to AMs and notified a few customers who asked. no escalations.
Tara (CSOps): retro items: - make enqueue+idempotency atomic or use leader-ordered queue - add unit test simulating sub-2s retry window in CI - add alert: duplicate-send-rate > 0.1% per hour - run a weekly sweep to detect potential duplicates across regions. Evan/Maya create tickets.
Maya (Data): created tickets CS-8590 (enqueue-idempotency-tests) and CS-8591 (duplicate-detection-sweep).
Evan (Scheduling): canary passed. rolling change to remaining workers now. monitoring queue and email delivery.
SchedulerBot: rollout completed at 2026-04-02T19:40:00Z (rollout_id=roll-102) :white_check_mark:
Tara (CSOps): monitoring shows duplicate-send-rate back to baseline. closing loop: 34 impacted, 8 re-enqueued surveys, no outstanding failures. i'll add runbook note and put ticket links in #cs-ops-docs. thanks all :heart:
